samples.claim: For Struct/Struct, List/List or Map/Map, intersection recurses over Self children in Self order, finds matching Other names, and filter_map discards every recursive error through .ok()?. Consequently strict intersection can silently omit a child with incompatible type and still succeed, even with empty children. Parent properties remain Self's, except id selects Self when nonnegative else Other; parent_id is not similarly selected. LargeList and FixedSizeList do not enter this recursive branch. Other strict mismatched types error; otherwise whole-field choice follows id sign. Public intersection and intersection_ignore_types forward false/true respectively.
samples.review_note: Original claim omitted the blob Self.clone short-circuit before matching-container recursion. Freshly reread913-1011, corrected current L2/L1/L3 and ledger analysis_record; original sampled text retained here as historical evidence.
samples.corrected_claim: After the preceding name/blob guards, Struct/Struct, List/List and Map/Map enter the matching-container branch. It first returns Self.clone() unchanged when Self is a blob, preserving its descriptor layout without child intersection or ID replacement. Otherwise it recurses over Self children in Self order, finds matching Other names, and filter_map discards every recursive error through .ok()?. Consequently strict intersection can silently omit an incompatible child and still succeed with empty children. Non-blob parent properties remain Self's except id selects Self when nonnegative else Other; parent_id is not similarly selected. LargeList and FixedSizeList do not enter this recursive branch. Outside it, strict mismatched types or different names return Error::arrow; name mismatch was already rejected at method entry. Otherwise whole-field choice follows id sign. Public intersection and intersection_ignore_types forward false/true respectively. (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:913-1011)

samples.claim: Page buffers need not be contiguous, though grouping is recommended for performance. Large pages mitigate seek/request overhead; the comment advises at least 8 MB and flushing when accumulated data is excessive, not a mandatory hard minimum. Concrete encodings are extensions. The ideal of adding plugins without recompilation is explicitly aspirational, not evidence of an implemented dynamic plugin registry.
samples.evidence:
97 |  * ## Data Pages
98 |  *
99 |  * A lot of flexibility is provided in how data is stored.  A page's buffers do
100 |  * not strictly need to be contiguous on the disk.  However, it is recommended
101 |  * that buffers within a page be grouped together for best performance.
102 |  *
103 |  * Data pages should be large.  The only time a page should be written to disk
104 |  * is when the writer needs to flush the page to disk because it has accumulated
105 |  * too much data.  Pages are not read in sequential order and if pages are too
106 |  * small then the seek overhead (or request overhead) will be problematic.  We
107 |  * generally advise that pages be at least 8MB or larger.
108 |  *
109 |  * ## Encodings
110 |  *
111 |  * Specific encodings are not part of this minimal format.  They are provided
112 |  * by extensions. Readers and writers should be designed so that encodings can
113 |  * be easily added and removed. Ideally, they should allow for this without
